correctness.rationale: At t=1 the step density is 2 times the positive-real-part hemisphere indicator, so the probability-TV distance is 1/2. For any nonnegative radial decreasing functions on S^3, layer cake reduces convolution monotonicity to overlap of two geodesic caps; conditioning on projection length onto the centers’ plane makes this the monotone intersection length of circular arcs for separations in [0,pi], including long arcs. Hence all f_t are radial nonincreasing. The mean-zero odd antipodal component h=2*1_H-1 satisfies f_t=1+h^{*t}, so f_t(q)+f_t(-q)=2 and H is exactly the positive set of f_t-1. For SU(2), character chi_n=sin((n+1)theta)/sin(theta), Haar radial weight 2sin²(theta)/pi, and central Fourier transform give zero for even nontrivial sectors and lambda_k=(-1)^k 4/[pi(2k+1)(2k+3)] at dimension 2k+2. Integrating the character series over H yields TV(t)=1/2 sum (2k+2)^2 lambda_k^(t+1), absolutely convergent at t=1. Direct hemisphere overlap gives f_2=2(1-theta/pi) and TV(2)=1/4-1/pi²; spectral dominance gives asymptotic (8/(3pi))(4/(3pi))^t. Independent Simpson quadrature and truncated absolutely convergent series gave TV2=0.14867881635766222 and 0.14867881635763006 respectively; these finite checks corroborate, not replace, the cap-overlap and spectral proof.
